note: The World Inequality Database (WID.world, bulk download of 15 October 2026, read again in that of 30 October 2026), Singapore, 2024: average net personal wealth (ahweal992j) and average post-tax national income (adiinc992j) per adult over 20, resources split equally within couples, in SGD of that year, for the bottom 20, 40, 60, 90 and 99 percent and the top 1 percent; each family's band is read from them. Read 2026-10-30. Read again 2026-11-03 from the bulk download of 30 October 2026 (its country files dated 30 October 2026): every row quoted here, its year and its currency label stood as before, and no later year was given. Until 2026-11-03 this note and its sources wrote the variable codes with their age and population parts swapped (ahwealj992 for ahweal992j and adiincj992 for adiinc992j), codes no file of the database holds (its README: type, concept, age group, population, as in sptinc992j), and called adiinc992j post-tax disposable income, which its metadata names post-tax national income ([Post-tax national income]=[Post-tax disposable income]+[Public spending]). The national accounts (the owner's ruling of 2026-11-03: each band's income scaled by households' disposable income over national income), searched again on 2026-11-03 in the statistics office's own accounts: SingStat's Table Builder, M016081 and M015031 (Personal Disposable Income and Saving, Second Quarter 2026, for the definition), 2024: the personal disposable income of households with the non-profit institutions serving them (S.14+S.15, nothing narrower published), 367,264.8, derived as the sum of the four quarters published (93,827.4; 85,087.7; 88,696; 99,653.7), and gross national income (B.5g) 632,874.6, in millions of Singapore dollars, a ratio of about 0.580 (`cash`). Gross over gross: the personal income was built from gross operating surplus, and SingStat published no consumption of fixed capital by sector and no net national income. Until 2026-11-03 each band's income was the database's post-tax national income as it stood, public spending included.

sources.title: Singapore Department of Statistics, SingStat Table Builder M016081 "Personal Disposable Income At Current Prices, Quarterly" (Non-seasonally Adjusted; data last updated 25/08/2026) and M015031 "Gross National Income, National Saving And Investment At Current Prices, Annual"; definition from SingStat "Personal Disposable Income and Saving, Second Quarter 2026" (https://www.singstat.gov.sg/files/c243775c-2ca9-42ed-b1c4-d18717e15cf2.pdf) and "Understanding the Differences between Personal Disposable Income and Household Market Income" (https://www.singstat.gov.sg/files/3018444e-ec2c-4b3f-836a-5126ad1bb9c1.pdf): table M016081 (https://tablebuilder.singstat.gov.sg/table/TS/M016081), through the API
sources.said: M016081 "Personal Disposable Income (Nominal) | Million Dollars": 2024 1Q 93827.4; 2024 2Q 85087.7; 2024 3Q 88696; 2024 4Q 99653.7 (2025 1Q 98299.1; 2Q 88342.1; 3Q 92376.1; 4Q 100633.1). Definition: "Personal disposable income (PDI) measures the income (e.g., compensation of employees, self-employment income) of the personal sector (i.e., households and non-profit institutions serving households (NPISHs)), after accounting for net investment income received (e.g., interest and dividends), net current transfers received (e.g., CPF top-ups and donations) and personal income tax paid." Key components listed: "Gross operating surplus (GOS) on NPISHs", "GOS on self-employment", "Imputed rental income from housing".
